Anna — thanks for sending. A couple of technical items we need called out explicitly in the consolidated quote (these drive sizing/costs):

- Concurrency scaling profile used to calculate compute: what assumed average and 95th percentile concurrency are you modeling for our account?
- Auto-suspend/auto-resume behavior for serverless warehouses and any implications for short-lived burst jobs (we run 30–90s pipelines frequently).
- Cross-region replication pricing: we need an explicit delta for storage vs egress vs compute so we can budget replication between us-west and eu-west.
- Long-term storage compression assumptions and the applied discounts (we currently keep 12 months hot, 24 months warm).

Also: if consolidation requires switching to Marketplace billing to combine Looker charges, outline the invoicing flow and any delayed recognition issues — finance will want to see this (Neha).

From a strategic perspective, we're assessing options to reduce unit costs without sacrificing latency for hot reads. If Snowflake can provide per-query latency baselines at our observed concurrency curves, that helps the case.

Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa / Vivek — following up on our quick sync. Attached is a draft SOW and high-level estimate for the consolidation work (SOW_Data_Platform_Consolidation_v1.docx). Highlights:

- Scope: inventory Looker content, rationalize explores/dashboards, map access controls, migrate critical derived tables to Snowflake-managed materialized views, and establish CI for LookML.
- Timeline: 8–10 weeks with a two-person engagement (lead PM + senior engineer).
- Cost: fixed-fee $98,000 (includes two knowledge-transfer sessions and one month of hypercare).
- Risks: LookML cleanup required in several folders; estimate assumes <20 complex explores. If more than 20, there will be adjustment.

Marissa — if Snowflake will provide a PS credit (per Anna's note), we can apply that against this SOW. Let me know whether you prefer we invoice Snowflake directly or Redwood for the work.
